chapter: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
title: Buffalo and the Asch record date with Hawkins
summary: The cold two weeks at McCann's in Buffalo and the Asch session including 'Sportsman's Hop' and 'Bean Stalkin'' that led to Capitol dates.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: But that's... I stayed with Hawk, and we went from here to...from New York to Buffalo for two weeks. And boy, was it cold up there. I thought New York was bad, but New York was like Los Angeles is compared to what Buffalo was. It was so cold, man, like we'd go to work every night and the cabs wouldn't even run! And the streets would be all...they had the snow drifts and everything. And man, like, we had a helluva time getting somebody to drive us back to the hotel and drive us back out there the next night.
Where were you working in Buffalo?
At McCann's Nightclub. Now, where did we stay for that two weeks, man...
Had you already done the record date for Asch?
Yeah, we'd already done that. We did that before we left here. Yeah, that turned out pretty nice.
You did a couple of originals on that, didn't you.
"Lullaby In Rhythm" -- I let Sir Charles
take credit for that one.
What did he call that, "Ladies' Lullaby"?
No, "Sportsman's Hop".
That's "Sportsman's Hop"?
Yeah. "Ladies' Lullaby" was Sir Charles' tune.
Oh, that was his tune, right.
Yeah.
Then of course, there was "Bean Stalkin'", which was...

Which was Bean's. Yeah, so that date turned out pretty good with Bean, which was nice. I think that's what got us the dates at Capitol, when we got out to California, because Dave Dexter had heard some of the tracks, I think, and he wanted to record the band. He was interested in...
Actually, that Asch record was some of the first...
Yeah, Bop...
...Bop things, along with, I guess, the thing...that "Woody'N You" that Hawk did with Diz...
Yeah.
But this album definitely had the new thing in it.
Yeah, he had the new mood of music.
But I guess some people who might not have accepted it, did accept it because it was Coleman Hawkins.
